cues.zh: Stuxnet 计算机蠕虫背后的思路
cues.en: The idea behind the Stuxnet computer worm
is actually quite simple.

cues.zh: 我们不想让伊朗拿到核弹。
cues.en: We don't want Iran to get the bomb.

cues.zh: 他们发展核武器的主要资产
cues.en: Their major asset for developing nuclear weapons
is the Natanz uranium enrichment facility.

cues.zh: 你看到的那些灰色盒子，
cues.en: The gray boxes that you see,
these are real-time control systems.

cues.zh: 如果我们能攻破这些系统
cues.en: Now if we manage to compromise these systems

cues.zh: 它们控制着驱动速度和阀门，
cues.en: that control drive speeds and valves,
we can actually cause a lot of problems
with the centrifuge.

cues.zh: 这些灰色盒子并不运行 Windows 软件；
cues.en: The gray boxes don't run Windows software;

cues.zh: 它们是完全不同的技术。
cues.en: they are a completely different technology.
But if we manage

cues.zh: 把一个好的 Windows 病毒
cues.en: to place a good Windows virus
on a notebook

cues.zh: 这台笔记本被维护工程师使用
cues.en: that is used by a maintenance engineer

cues.zh: 用来配置这个灰色盒子，
cues.en: to configure this gray box,
then we are in business.

cues.zh: 这就是 Stuxnet 背后的阴谋。
cues.en: And this is the plot behind Stuxnet.

cues.zh: 所以我们从一个 Windows 投放器开始。
cues.en: So we start with a Windows dropper.
The payload goes onto the gray box,
damages the centrifuge,
and the Iranian nuclear program is delayed --
mission accomplished.
That's easy, huh?

cues.zh: 我想告诉你们我们是怎么发现的。
cues.en: I want to tell you how we found that out.

cues.zh: 六个月前我们刚开始研究 Stuxnet 时，
cues.en: When we started our research on Stuxnet six months ago,

cues.zh: 完全不知道这东西的目的是什么。
cues.en: it was completely unknown what the purpose of this thing was.
The only thing that was known

cues.zh: 它在 Windows 部分、投放器部分非常非常复杂，
cues.en: is it's very, very complex on the Windows part, the dropper part,
used multiple zero-day vulnerabilities.

cues.zh: 而且它似乎想对这些灰色盒子、
cues.en: And it seemed to want to do something

cues.zh: 这些实时控制系统做些什么。
cues.en: with these gray boxes, these real-time control systems.
So that got our attention,

cues.zh: 我们启动了一个实验室项目
cues.en: and we started a lab project

cues.zh: 我们在自己的环境中感染了 Stuxnet
cues.en: where we infected our environment with Stuxnet

cues.zh: 然后研究了一下这东西。
cues.en: and checked this thing out.

cues.zh: 接着发生了些非常有趣的事。
cues.en: And then some very funny things happened.

cues.zh: Stuxnet 表现得像只实验室老鼠
cues.en: Stuxnet behaved like a lab rat
that didn't like our cheese --
sniffed, but didn't want to eat.
Didn't make sense to me.

cues.zh: 在我们尝试了不同口味的奶酪之后，
cues.en: And after we experimented with different flavors of cheese,

cues.zh: 我意识到，这是一次定向攻击。
cues.en: I realized, well, this is a directed attack.
It's completely directed.
The dropper is prowling actively
on the gray box
if a specific configuration is found,

cues.zh: 甚至即使它试图感染的实际程序代码
cues.en: and even if the actual program code that it's trying to infect

cues.zh: 确实在那台目标机器上运行。
cues.en: is actually running on that target.

cues.zh: 如果没有，Stuxnet 就什么都不做。
cues.en: And if not, Stuxnet does nothing.

cues.zh: 这确实引起了我的注意，
cues.en: So that really got my attention,

cues.zh: 于是我们开始着手研究
cues.en: and we started to work on this

cues.zh: 几乎是日夜不停地工作，
cues.en: nearly around the clock,

cues.zh: 因为我想：“好吧，我们不知道目标是什么。
cues.en: because I thought, "Well, we don't know what the target is.
It could be, let's say for example,
a U.S. power plant,

cues.zh: 或者德国的一家化工厂。
cues.en: or a chemical plant in Germany.

cues.zh: 所以我们最好尽快查明目标是什么。”
cues.en: So we better find out what the target is soon."

cues.zh: 于是我们提取并反编译了
cues.en: So we extracted and decompiled
the attack code,

cues.zh: 发现它由两个数字炸弹构成——
cues.en: and we discovered that it's structured in two digital bombs --

cues.zh: 一个较小的和一个较大的。
cues.en: a smaller one and a bigger one.

cues.zh: 我们还看出它们的设计非常专业，
cues.en: And we also saw that they are very professionally engineered

cues.zh: 显然出自掌握全部内幕信息的人之手。
cues.en: by people who obviously had all insider information.

cues.zh: 他们掌握了所有必要的信息
cues.en: They knew all the bits and bites

cues.zh: 那些他们必须攻击的环节。
cues.en: that they had to attack.

cues.zh: 他们甚至可能知道操作员的鞋码。
cues.en: They probably even know the shoe size of the operator.
So they know everything.

cues.zh: 如果你听说过Stuxnet的投放器
cues.en: And if you have heard that the dropper of Stuxnet
is complex and high-tech,
let me tell you this:

cues.zh: 其有效载荷简直是火箭科学。
cues.en: the payload is rocket science.
It's way above everything
that we have ever seen before.

cues.zh: 这里展示的是实际攻击代码的一个样本。
cues.en: Here you see a sample of this actual attack code.
We are talking about --
around about 15,000 lines of code.

cues.zh: 看起来很像老式的汇编语言。
cues.en: Looks pretty much like old-style assembly language.

cues.zh: 我想告诉你我们是如何
cues.en: And I want to tell you how we were able
to make sense out of this code.

cues.zh: 所以我们首先寻找的是系统函数调用，
cues.en: So what we were looking for is, first of all, system function calls,

cues.zh: 因为我们知道它们的作用。
cues.en: because we know what they do.

cues.zh: 接着我们寻找定时器和数据结构，
cues.en: And then we were looking for timers and data structures

cues.zh: 并试图将它们与现实世界——
cues.en: and trying to relate them to the real world --

cues.zh: 与潜在的现实世界目标联系起来。
cues.en: to potential real world targets.

cues.zh: 所以确实需要目标理论
cues.en: So we do need target theories

cues.zh: 能让我们去证实或证伪。
cues.en: that we can prove or disprove.
In order to get target theories,
we remember

cues.zh: 这绝对是硬核破坏行动，
cues.en: that it's definitely hardcore sabotage,
it must be a high-value target
and it is most likely located in Iran,

cues.zh: 因为大部分感染都报告在那里。
cues.en: because that's where most of the infections had been reported.

cues.zh: 可你没法在那片区域找到几千个目标。
cues.en: Now you don't find several thousand targets in that area.
It basically boils down
to the Bushehr nuclear power plant
and to the Natanz fuel enrichment plant.
So I told my assistant,

cues.zh: “从我们的客户库里，把所有离心机和电厂专家的名单给我。”
cues.en: "Get me a list of all centrifuge and power plant experts from our client base."

cues.zh: 我给他们打电话，汲取他们的见解
cues.en: And I phoned them up and picked their brain

cues.zh: 努力把他们的专业知识
cues.en: in an effort to match their expertise

cues.zh: 与我们在代码和数据中发现的东西对应起来。
cues.en: with what we found in code and data.
And that worked pretty well.
So we were able to associate
the small digital warhead
with the rotor control.

cues.zh: 转子是离心机里的运动部件，
cues.en: The rotor is that moving part within the centrifuge,

cues.zh: 就是你们看到的那个黑色物体。
cues.en: that black object that you see.

cues.zh: 如果你操纵这个转子的转速，
cues.en: And if you manipulate the speed of this rotor,

cues.zh: 你实际上就能让转子产生裂纹，
cues.en: you are actually able to crack the rotor

cues.zh: 最终甚至让离心机爆炸。
cues.en: and eventually even have the centrifuge explode.
What we also saw
is that the goal of the attack

cues.zh: 其实就是要缓慢而诡异地进行——
cues.en: was really to do it slowly and creepy --
obviously in an effort
to drive maintenance engineers crazy,

cues.zh: 让他们无法迅速查明原因。
cues.en: that they would not be able to figure this out quickly.

cues.zh: 这个大型数字弹头——我们之所以能有所发现，
cues.en: The big digital warhead -- we had a shot at this

cues.zh: 是因为我们非常仔细地
cues.en: by looking very closely

cues.zh: 研究了数据和数据结构。
cues.en: at data and data structures.
So for example, the number 164

cues.zh: 在那段代码里非常显眼；
cues.en: really stands out in that code;
you can't overlook it.
I started to research scientific literature
on how these centrifuges

cues.zh: 在纳坦兹究竟是如何建造的，
cues.en: are actually built in Natanz
and found they are structured

cues.zh: 所谓的级联结构组织的，
cues.en: in what is called a cascade,

cues.zh: 每个级联包含164台离心机。
cues.en: and each cascade holds 164 centrifuges.

cues.zh: 这就说得通了，两者是匹配的。
cues.en: So that made sense, that was a match.
And it even got better.
These centrifuges in Iran
are subdivided into 15, what is called, stages.

cues.zh: 你猜我们在攻击代码里发现了什么？
cues.en: And guess what we found in the attack code?
An almost identical structure.

cues.zh: 所以这又是一次非常吻合的匹配。
cues.en: So again, that was a real good match.

cues.zh: 这让我们对眼前看到的东西有了很高的信心。
cues.en: And this gave us very high confidence for what we were looking at.

cues.zh: 别误会，过程可不是这么一帆风顺的。
cues.en: Now don't get me wrong here, it didn't go like this.
These results have been obtained

cues.zh: 经过好几周极其艰苦的工作才得到的。
cues.en: over several weeks of really hard labor.
And we often went into just a dead end
and had to recover.
Anyway, so we figured out
that both digital warheads

cues.zh: 其实瞄准的是同一个目标，
cues.en: were actually aiming at one and the same target,
but from different angles.
The small warhead is taking one cascade,
and spinning up the rotors and slowing them down,
and the big warhead
is talking to six cascades
and manipulating valves.
So in all, we are very confident

cues.zh: 我们已经确定了目标是什么。
cues.en: that we have actually determined what the target is.

cues.zh: 是纳坦兹，而且只是纳坦兹。
cues.en: It is Natanz, and it is only Natanz.
So we don't have to worry
that other targets
might be hit by Stuxnet.

cues.zh: 我们看到的是一些非常酷的东西——
cues.en: Here's some very cool stuff that we saw --
really knocked my socks off.
Down there is the gray box,

cues.zh: 上面你看到的是离心机。
cues.en: and on the top you see the centrifuges.
Now what this thing does

cues.zh: 拦截来自传感器的输入值——
cues.en: is it intercepts the input values from sensors --
so for example, from pressure sensors
and vibration sensors --

cues.zh: 并向仍在运行的合法程序代码
cues.en: and it provides legitimate program code,
which is still running during the attack,

cues.zh: 这些代码在攻击期间仍在运行。
cues.en: with fake input data.

cues.zh: 事实上，这些伪造的输入数据
cues.en: And as a matter of fact, this fake input data

cues.zh: 实际上是由震网预先录制的。
cues.en: is actually prerecorded by Stuxnet.

cues.zh: 所以就像好莱坞电影里那样
cues.en: So it's just like from the Hollywood movies
where during the heist,

cues.zh: 监控摄像头被喂以预先录制的视频。
cues.en: the observation camera is fed with prerecorded video.
That's cool, huh?
The idea here is obviously

cues.zh: 不只是骗过控制室里的操作员。
cues.en: not only to fool the operators in the control room.

cues.zh: 实际上它更危险、更具攻击性。
cues.en: It actually is much more dangerous and aggressive.
The idea
is to circumvent a digital safety system.

cues.zh: 我们需要数字安全系统，
cues.en: We need digital safety systems

cues.zh: 因为人类操作员来不及反应。
cues.en: where a human operator could not act quick enough.
So for example, in a power plant,

cues.zh: 当大型蒸汽轮机转速过高时，
cues.en: when your big steam turbine gets too over speed,

cues.zh: 必须在毫秒内打开泄压阀。
cues.en: you must open relief valves within a millisecond.

cues.zh: 显然，人类操作员做不到。
cues.en: Obviously, this cannot be done by a human operator.

cues.zh: 所以这里就需要数字安全系统。
cues.en: So this is where we need digital safety systems.
And when they are compromised,

cues.zh: 真正糟糕的事情就会发生。
cues.en: then real bad things can happen.
Your plant can blow up.

cues.zh: 而操作员和安全系统都不会察觉。
cues.en: And neither your operators nor your safety system will notice it.
That's scary.
But it gets worse.

cues.zh: 我接下来要说的非常重要。
cues.en: And this is very important, what I'm going to say.
Think about this:
this attack is generic.
It doesn't have anything to do, in specifics,
with centrifuges,
with uranium enrichment.

cues.zh: 所以它同样适用于，比如说，
cues.en: So it would work as well, for example,
in a power plant
or in an automobile factory.
It is generic.

cues.zh: 而且作为攻击者，你不需要——
cues.en: And you don't have -- as an attacker --
you don't have to deliver this payload
by a USB stick,

cues.zh: 正如我们在 Stuxnet 案例中看到的那样。
cues.en: as we saw it in the case of Stuxnet.

cues.zh: 你也可以用传统的蠕虫技术来传播。
cues.en: You could also use conventional worm technology for spreading.
Just spread it as wide as possible.
And if you do that,
what you end up with

cues.zh: 就是一种大规模杀伤性网络武器。
cues.en: is a cyber weapon of mass destruction.
That's the consequence
that we have to face.
So unfortunately,

cues.zh: 这类攻击的最大目标数量
cues.en: the biggest number of targets for such attacks
are not in the Middle East.

cues.zh: 而是在美国、欧洲和日本。
cues.en: They're in the United States and Europe and in Japan.

cues.zh: 所以所有这些绿色区域，
cues.en: So all of the green areas,
these are your target-rich environments.
We have to face the consequences,

cues.zh: 而且最好现在就开始准备。
cues.en: and we better start to prepare right now.
Thanks.
(Applause)
Chris Anderson: I've got a question.
Ralph, it's been quite widely reported
that people assume that Mossad
is the main entity behind this.
Is that your opinion?
Ralph Langner: Okay, you really want to hear that?
Yeah. Okay.

cues.zh: 我的看法是，Mossad确实参与其中，
cues.en: My opinion is that the Mossad is involved,

cues.zh: 但主导力量并不是以色列。
cues.en: but that the leading force is not Israel.
So the leading force behind that
is the cyber superpower.
There is only one,
and that's the United States --
fortunately, fortunately.
Because otherwise,
our problems would even be bigger.

cues.zh: CA：谢谢你把我们吓得魂飞魄散。谢谢你，Ralph。
cues.en: CA: Thank you for scaring the living daylights out of us. Thank you, Ralph.
(Applause)
